subject: System Design
title: The GitHub DDoS Attack of 2018
description: A quick win: understand The GitHub DDoS Attack of 2018.

hook.text: On February 28, 2018, GitHub was hit with 1.35 Tbps of traffic — the largest DDoS attack ever recorded at the time.

buildup.text: Attackers used memcached amplification: small requests to open memcached servers returned massive responses.

discovery.text: Each 15-byte request was amplified into a 750 KB response — a 51,000x amplification factor.

twist.text: GitHub was back online in 10 minutes. Their DDoS mitigation partner, Akamai, absorbed the traffic.

climax.text: The attack was massive, but preparation and a strong mitigation partner made recovery remarkably fast.

punchline.text: 1.35 Tbps of attack traffic, 10 minutes to recover.

quiz.question: What amplification factor did the GitHub DDoS attack use?
